facts.fact: A Muse Code subscription is a flat monthly rate for usage of Muse Code, instead of paying per token.
facts.quote: With a Muse Code subscription, you pay a flat monthly rate for usage of Muse Code, instead of paying per token.

facts.fact: Muse Code has 4 subscription plans: Everyday Usage, High Usage, Power Usage, and Maximum Usage.
facts.quote: There are 4 subscription plans available for Muse Code:

facts.fact: The Everyday Usage plan lets subscribers send 10-50 prompts every 5 hours, including image and video uploads.
facts.quote: Send 10-50 prompts every 5 hours, including image and video uploads

facts.fact: The High Usage plan provides 5x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan.
facts.quote: 5x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan

facts.fact: The Power Usage plan provides 20x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan and includes access to Muse Wonder Full.
facts.quote: 20x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan

facts.fact: The Maximum Usage plan provides 80x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan.
facts.quote: 80x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan

facts.fact: Subscribers must be 18 or the age of majority in their country to subscribe to Muse Code.
facts.quote: You must be 18 or the age of majority in your country to subscribe.

facts.fact: Muse Code subscriptions default to Contributor mode, which gives more plan usage in exchange for letting Meta use content to train future Meta models.
facts.quote: Muse Code subscriptions default to Contributor mode.

facts.fact: The subscription applies only to the Muse Code API key automatically connected during CLI onboarding; additional API keys are billed pay-as-you-go.
facts.quote: Any additional API keys you create under your Meta Model API account will be billed through pay-as-you-go.

facts.fact: A plan upgrade takes effect immediately, and the subscriber is charged a prorated amount for the rest of the current billing cycle.
facts.quote: A plan upgrade takes effect immediately. You will be charged a prorated amount for the rest of the current billing cycle.

facts.fact: A plan downgrade takes effect at the start of the next billing cycle, and the current plan's usage limit remains until then.
facts.quote: A plan downgrade takes effect at the start of your next billing cycle.

facts.fact: A canceled subscription stays active until the end of the current billing cycle.
facts.quote: Your subscription stays active until the end of the current billing cycle, then you lose access to all benefits.

facts.fact: To avoid future charges, a subscription must be canceled at least 24 hours before the next billing date.
facts.quote: Cancel at least 24 hours before your next billing date to avoid future charges.

facts.fact: Deactivating an account keeps the subscription active for 30 days before Meta revokes it if not reactivated.
facts.quote: Deactivating your account keeps the subscription active for 30 days.

facts.fact: Deleting an account cancels the subscription immediately.
facts.quote: deleting your account cancels the subscription immediately.

facts.fact: Meta may revoke a subscription after a payment failure when the payment method fails and no backup payment method is on file.
facts.quote: your payment method fails and you have no backup payment method on file.

facts.fact: Contributor mode can be turned on or off per run with the --contributor-mode flag or the MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE environment variable (1 for on, 0 for off), and the flag takes precedence if both are set.
facts.quote: You can also set the environment variable MUSE_CONTRIBUTOR_MODE to 1 (on) or 0 (off) for a run. If you set both, the flag wins.

facts.fact: The subscription renews automatically each month on the date the user first subscribed.
facts.quote: Your subscription renews automatically each month on the date you first subscribed.

facts.fact: If the subscription's original renewal date does not exist in a given month, the user is charged on the last day of that month instead.
facts.quote: If that date doesn't exist in a given month (for example, the 31st in a 30-day month), you're charged on the last day of that month instead.

facts.fact: Canceling a subscription does not earn a credit or refund unless required by law.
facts.quote: if you cancel your subscription, you won't receive a credit or refund unless required by law.
